findings.reason: one owner must be named (either §51's sentence points at `sib-catalog-consistency` in §52, or the node leaves §52's list); otherwise the pass is either duplicated at cost or never dispatched.
findings.text: `sib-catalog-consistency` is listed among §52's nodes ("one pass over the families the full run and the cohort reruns created, so that each concept has one definition, one documentation template and one grouping"), but §51 ends by saying "A catalog-consistency pass over the families the two runs created follows as its own node once this section closes" (line 301): the same deliverable is now owned inside §52 and by a separate node §51 defers to, so a dispatcher reading either section can start it twice or each section can wait on the other

findings.reason: without a bullet per node (and a planted surviving cycle as the repair's control) the section can be closed with the lineage cycles unrepaired and the consistency pass undone, which is the two-node prerequisite the lead's 2026-11-09 ruling makes the scale-up wait on.
findings.text: the section declares four nodes but its done-when covers three of the four: bullet 1 and bullet 3 measure `sib-unaccepted-census`, bullet 2 measures `sib-full-dd-continuation` and bullet 4 the export gate, and nothing measures `sib-lineage-cycle-repair`'s "leaving the census of cycles at zero" or `sib-catalog-consistency`'s "each concept has one definition, one documentation template and one grouping", both of which are graph mutations on the live catalog (the census recorded 144 cycle names in 68 groups and 18 multi-tip lineages) carrying no control

findings.reason: the other three nodes in this section each name their entry point (`sn run`, `sn edit`, the graph read), so naming the repair's path (or declaring the operation it needs built, with its own test) is what makes the node dispatchable at all.
findings.text: `sib-lineage-cycle-repair` says it "repairs each through the signed successor path with a receipt" but names no command, module or function, and no such path exists: `imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_ordering.py:186 _find_cyclic_components` only detects cycles and withholds them from catalog ordering, and `imas_codex/standard_names/edit.py` carries fold, reclaim and spelling operations (`_FOLD_LINEAGE_OPERATIONS`, `_reclaim_spelling_case`) with no cycle-repair case, so a dispatcher must either invent a write path for 144 cycle names or reach for direct Cypher, which the repository's standard-names rules forbid

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `imas-standard-names:dd-gap-vocabulary#s4` resolves: the href's project prefix is imas-standard-names, where `docs/plans/dd-gap-vocabulary.html` exists and carries `id="s4"` (the grammar release section); `c-s51-lead-rulings-2026-11-09` is present as a `_top` comment in the same document, and the fragments directory named in bullet 1 resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §52's done-when measures only the census, the continuation and the export gate; neither `sib-lineage-cycle-repair` nor `sib-catalog-consistency`, both declared as this section's nodes, has a section-level bar or a negative control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the census JSON and fragment are placed under `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/`, a directory that exists in the repository and holds this plan's other gate fragments.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the added node ids and prose carry no ticket numbers, stage labels or changelog references, and name their mechanisms by what they do.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — `sib-lineage-cycle-repair` names no command, module or caller for its write, and no such operation exists in the tree, so the mechanism the section relies on for zero lineage cycles does not run on any real code path as written.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the four declared nodes are one goal (the remaining DD reaching accepted names) with the lead's 2026-11-09 ruling naming the repair and consistency pass as ordered preconditions of the scale-up (`c-s51-lead-rulings-2026-11-09`, line 322), which matches the section's titles and node order.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — `sib-catalog-consistency` is declared as one of §52's four nodes (docs/plans/sn-integrity-backlog.html:305), while §51's closing sentence hands the same pass to a separate future node over the same families (docs/plans/sn-integrity-backlog.html:301), so the deliverable has two owners.
